papers_read.title_as_printed: Machine Learning-Based Prediction Models for Cognitive Decline Progression: A Comparative Study in Multilingual Settings Using Speech Analysis (Ceyhan, Bek, Onal-Suzek, J Aging Res & Lifestyle 2024)
Linguistic-based Mild Cognitive Impairment detection using Informative Loss (Pourramezan Fard et al., Computers in Biology and Medicine 2024)

what_each_reports.P-158: Acoustic features (MFCC, RMS, ZCR, spectral) from Cookie Theft recordings; ADReSS (AD vs non-AD, English): random forest 95% accuracy under 10-fold CV on augmented 20-s segments (1520 samples from 153 recordings), but 73% on the ADReSS test set; MUDC (60 Turkish MCI-clinic patients): MLP 94%; cross-language 72%/76%.
what_each_reports.P-6: Transformer on ASR transcripts of semi-structured video-chat interviews, I-CONECT (68 subjects: 34 MCI, 34 NC), 5-fold subject-level CV: accuracy 85.16% (SD 5.76), AUC 84.75%; over 25 repeated fold configurations mean AUC 79.94%.

quantity_a: Classification accuracy for Alzheimer's dementia vs non-AD from acoustic features of picture-description speech (ADReSS/Pitt corpus), estimated by 10-fold CV over augmented segments.
quantity_b: Subject-level classification accuracy for MCI vs normal cognition from linguistic (transcript) features of conversational interviews (I-CONECT, age 75+).
incompatible_if_same: Possibly, 95% vs 85.16% (SD 5.76), but P-158's own held-out ADReSS test accuracy is 73%, below P-6, so even on its face the pairing does not show one result excluding the other.

gates.task: mismatch: P-158's 95% is dementia (AD) vs non-AD; P-6 is MCI vs NC.
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: ADReSS/DementiaBank Pitt vs I-CONECT (record itself says dataset_equal No).
gates.validation_tier: nominally matched (both internal CV), but P-158's CV is over speed-perturbed segments of the same recordings, while P-6's is subject-level.
gates.modality_family: match at family level (speech/language) but different input representation: acoustic signal features vs transcript text embeddings.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: both accuracy, but for different diagnostic contrasts (AD vs control vs MCI vs NC).
performance_validity: flag not tripped (95% < 0.97), but P-158's 95% is a segment-level CV on augmented data from 153 recordings with a 73% held-out test result, so it is a weak performance estimate in any case.
grounds: P-158's 95% accuracy separates Alzheimer's dementia from non-AD speakers, while P-6's 85.16% separates MCI from normal cognition, so the population behind the label differs.

The datasets (ADReSS vs I-CONECT), elicitation tasks (picture description vs conversational interviews) and input representations (acoustic features vs transcript embeddings) differ, and the dataset gate fails with no waiver.
P-158's own held-out ADReSS test accuracy is 73%, so the 95% figure is a CV estimate on augmented segments, not a comparable subject-level estimate.

evidence_quotes.quote: it is a balanced dataset composed of cognitively normal (CN) patients and those suffering from Alzheimer's disease (AD)
we programmatically perturbed each section at speeds of 0.7, 0.8, 1.2, and 1.3 to create 1520 samples from 153 samples for the training dataset
We achieved 73% accuracy for the labels (dementia or not) and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 5.6 for the MMSE predictions
Among the 68 randomized individuals, 34 were identified with MCI, while 34 were diagnosed with NC conditions.
the framework achieves an overall accuracy of 85.16% and an AUC of 84.75%, with the corresponding std of 5.76 and 5.97, respectively.

record_defects: Both claims labelled 'T1' as if the same MCI-detection task; P-158's 95% is AD-vs-non-AD on ADReSS.
resolution_note says 'Confirmed genuine: Same metric type (Acc)' while resolution says 'Rejected: Task, dataset, or modality mismatch'; the note's reasoning ignores the population difference.
claim_a still cites P-276 (repointed to P-158 on 2026-09-16).
C-169 is a duplicate of this record (same pair after the P-11 -> P-6 repoint).
Index registry row for P-6 gives Sample_N_Approx 151 and Task T2; the paper analyses 68 subjects (34 MCI/34 NC) in an MCI-vs-NC detection task.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A P-158 result for MCI vs normal cognition on subject-level validation (its MUDC set is all MCI-clinic patients stratified by MMSE, not MCI vs NC) would be needed to share P-6's estimand.
